questions.q: The editorial calls the present earth “a nursery.” What does it mean?
options: A place meant only for children
Not quite. The article says: A place where people are tested and prepared, so that those of noble character may be chosen for the eternal world.
A garden to be enjoyed without care
Not quite. The article says: A place where people are tested and prepared, so that those of noble character may be chosen for the eternal world.
A place where people are tested and prepared, so that those of noble character may be chosen for the eternal world
Yes. The true abode comes after.
A planet soon to be replaced by another in space
Not quite. The article says: A place where people are tested and prepared, so that those of noble character may be chosen for the eternal world.
questions.rationale: “The present earth is like a nursery where human beings are meant to be tested. The person who gives proof of noble conduct and sublime character… will be chosen to settle in the eternal world of the Hereafter.”

questions.q: “It is not ease but effort, not facility but difficulty that makes man.” How does the article explain why?
options: Easy tasks are usually forbidden
Not quite. The article says: The mind releases more energy for a difficult task, and this builds a strong personality.
Difficult tasks earn more praise
Not quite. The article says: The mind releases more energy for a difficult task, and this builds a strong personality.
Difficulty makes people fear failure
Not quite. The article says: The mind releases more energy for a difficult task, and this builds a strong personality.
The mind releases more energy for a difficult task, and this builds a strong personality
Right. A high target opens the reservoir wider.
questions.rationale: “If we decide to do some difficult or great task, then the mind will release a greater amount of energy.”

questions.article: Peace Is Possible, but Only Through the Right Way
questions.q: “You cannot extinguish a fire by pouring fuel on it.” What is the wider lesson?
options: Results come only by following the principles God has set, such as patience and positive action, not by emotional methods of our own
Well read. The world does not accept excuses.
Strong feeling is the proof of sincerity
Not quite. The article says: Results come only by following the principles God has set, such as patience and positive action, not by emotional methods of our own.
Fires should be left to burn out
Not quite. The article says: Results come only by following the principles God has set, such as patience and positive action, not by emotional methods of our own.
Every problem needs outside help
Not quite. The article says: Results come only by following the principles God has set, such as patience and positive action, not by emotional methods of our own.
questions.rationale: “If God has made patience the secret of success in this world of His, you cannot attain success through impatience.”

questions.article: Peace Is Possible, but Only Through the Right Way
questions.q: The article says man’s freedom is “of action alone.” What has he not been given?
options: The chance to try again
Not quite. The article says: Power over the results of his actions.
The right to choose
Not quite. The article says: Power over the results of his actions.
The ability to think
Not quite. The article says: Power over the results of his actions.
Power over the results of his actions
Exactly. One may dive in, but only a swimmer stays afloat.
questions.rationale: “We are free to do whatever we like to, but we have not been given the power to acquire the results that we seek.”

questions.q: Whom does the article call the “spiritual companions” of the Prophet?
options: Rulers who built mosques
Not quite. The article says: Sincere seekers of truth in any age who discover him through study and follow his example.
Only those who lived in Madinah
Not quite. The article says: Sincere seekers of truth in any age who discover him through study and follow his example.
Sincere seekers of truth in any age who discover him through study and follow his example
Yes. His guidance continues forever.
Authors of the books of history
Not quite. The article says: Sincere seekers of truth in any age who discover him through study and follow his example.
questions.rationale: “They were those honest people who were born as seekers of truth. Then they discovered the Prophet through further study, and decided to follow the pattern of his life.”

questions.q: “My mercy prevails over My anger.” What attitude does this create in a believer, according to the article?
options: Fear of accountability together with a hope that is stronger still
Correct. “They called on Us in hope and fear.”
Complete freedom from any fear
Not quite. The article says: Fear of accountability together with a hope that is stronger still.
Constant dread with little hope
Not quite. The article says: Fear of accountability together with a hope that is stronger still.
Indifference to his own mistakes
Not quite. The article says: Fear of accountability together with a hope that is stronger still.
questions.rationale: “Just as God’s mercy overcomes His wrath, when God’s servant thinks of his merciful Creator, his hope overwhelms his fear.”

questions.q: Why does the article say spirituality can be attained in every situation?
options: It depends only on one’s own sincerity and willpower, not on overcoming anyone else
Right. It is a matter of individual choice.
Because society always supports it
Not quite. The article says: It depends only on one’s own sincerity and willpower, not on overcoming anyone else.
Because it needs no effort at all
Not quite. The article says: It depends only on one’s own sincerity and willpower, not on overcoming anyone else.
Because it is the same as success in the world
Not quite. The article says: It depends only on one’s own sincerity and willpower, not on overcoming anyone else.
questions.rationale: “Spirituality is a target that is achievable in every situation, provided you are sincere and determined… It needs only one thing—and that is willpower.”

questions.q: Animals use camouflage, staying out of sight and other means to avoid a fight. How does the article judge such avoidance?
options: As proof that animals feel no danger
Not quite. The article says: As necessary pragmatism taught by nature, not cowardice – it lets constructive work continue.
As weakness that humans should not copy
Not quite. The article says: As necessary pragmatism taught by nature, not cowardice – it lets constructive work continue.
As a trick suited only to small creatures
Not quite. The article says: As necessary pragmatism taught by nature, not cowardice – it lets constructive work continue.
As necessary pragmatism taught by nature, not cowardice – it lets constructive work continue
Well reasoned. Humans should do by choice what animals do by instinct.
questions.rationale: “They are not a form or expression of cowardice. Rather, they indicate a necessary pragmatism.”

questions.q: Our surroundings condition our minds until we take our conditioning for the truth. What remedy does the article give?
options: Avoiding all discussion
Not quite. The article says: Constant introspection – becoming one’s own inspector.
Moving to a new place
Not quite. The article says: Constant introspection – becoming one’s own inspector.
Constant introspection – becoming one’s own inspector
Yes. Sorting what is natural from what is merely absorbed.
Following the majority view
Not quite. The article says: Constant introspection – becoming one’s own inspector.
questions.rationale: “We have to become our own inspector and must constantly inspect ourselves.”

questions.q: A Hadith gives greater reward to the believer who mixes with people and bears their annoyance patiently. What further benefit does the article see in such a life?
options: It leaves less time for worry
Not quite. The article says: Every interaction becomes a chance to learn and to develop one’s thinking.
Every interaction becomes a chance to learn and to develop one’s thinking
Well read. For one with the spirit of learning.
It helps in winning arguments
Not quite. The article says: Every interaction becomes a chance to learn and to develop one’s thinking.
It brings a wide circle of admirers
Not quite. The article says: Every interaction becomes a chance to learn and to develop one’s thinking.
questions.rationale: “Interaction with others provides a person the opportunity to reform his own thinking. One gains the chance to expand one’s knowledge.”
